intro.say: Weather is what the sky and air are like outside. Let's look out the window!

rounds.say: Sunny days are bright and warm. Rainy days have water falling from clouds.
rounds.caption: sunny · rainy

rounds.say: Cloudy days have lots of clouds. Snowy days are cold and white. Windy days blow things around!
rounds.caption: cloudy · snowy · windy

rounds.ask: Water is falling from the clouds. What is the weather?

options.label: sunny
options.why: Look, there is water falling. That's rain.

options.label: snowy
options.why: Snowflakes are white and fluffy. These are raindrops.

rounds.explain: Water falling from the clouds is rain.

rounds.ask: Which weather is good for making a snowman?

options.label: sunny
options.why: It's too warm for snow on a hot sunny day.

options.label: windy
options.why: Wind blows, but we need snow for a snowman.

rounds.explain: You need cold, snowy weather to build a snowman.

rounds.ask: The kite is flying high. What is the weather?

options.label: rainy
options.why: Rain makes things wet. Wind makes kites fly.

rounds.explain: Wind pushes the kite up into the sky.

rounds.ask: What do we wear? Sort each thing into sunny, rainy or snowy.
rounds.explain: We dress for the weather to stay cool, dry, or warm.

rounds.ask: It is sunny and hot. What should you wear?

options.label: scarf
options.why: A scarf is for cold days. On hot days, wear a sun hat.

rounds.explain: A sun hat keeps the hot sun off your head and face.

intro.say: A year has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. Each one has different weather.

rounds.say: In spring, it gets warmer. Flowers bloom and baby animals are born. In summer, it is hot and sunny.
rounds.caption: spring · summer

rounds.say: In autumn, it gets cooler and leaves fall from trees. In winter, it is cold, and in some places it snows.
rounds.caption: autumn · winter

rounds.ask: Put the seasons in order, starting with spring.
rounds.explain: Spring, summer, autumn, winter. Then spring comes again!

rounds.ask: Leaves are falling from the trees. What season is it?

options.label: summer
options.why: In summer, trees are full of green leaves.

options.label: spring
options.why: In spring, new leaves grow on trees.

rounds.explain: In autumn, leaves change color and fall from the trees.

rounds.ask: Is it summer or winter? Sort the pictures.
rounds.explain: Summer is hot, so we go to the beach. Winter is cold, so we wrap up warm.
After cold winter comes spring, when it gets warmer again.

rounds.ask: Flowers bloom and baby birds hatch. What season is it?

options.label: winter
options.why: Winter is cold. Flowers bloom when it warms up.

rounds.explain: Spring is when plants and animals start new life.

intro.say: Where does rain come from? How is a rainbow made? Let's find out, and learn to stay safe in a storm.

rounds.say: The Sun warms water in seas and puddles. It rises up as water vapour, too tiny to see, and makes clouds.
rounds.caption: water rises → clouds

rounds.say: When clouds get full and heavy, the water falls as rain. Then it goes back to the sea. This is the water cycle!
rounds.caption: the water cycle

rounds.say: A rainbow needs sunshine and raindrops at the same time. Sunlight shines through the drops and splits into colors.
rounds.caption: sun + rain = rainbow

rounds.ask: Put the water cycle in order.
rounds.explain: Water rises, makes clouds, falls as rain, and goes back. Then it starts again!
rounds.hint: Start with the Sun warming the water.

rounds.ask: What two things do you need to see a rainbow?

options.label: snow and wind
options.why: A rainbow needs sunlight shining through raindrops.

options.label: clouds and night
options.why: At night there is no sunlight to make a rainbow.

rounds.explain: Sunlight shining through raindrops makes a rainbow.

options.label: the Sun is sad
options.why: The Sun doesn't have feelings. Clouds rain when full of water.

options.label: the wind is cold
options.why: Wind moves clouds, but rain falls when clouds are full of water.

rounds.explain: Clouds are made of tiny water drops. When they get too heavy, they fall as rain.

rounds.ask: You see lightning and hear thunder. Where is the safest place to go?

options.label: under a tall tree
options.why: Lightning can hit tall trees. It's safer inside.

options.label: an open field
options.why: Open fields are not safe in a storm. Go inside.

rounds.explain: Going indoors is the safest thing to do in a thunderstorm.

rounds.ask: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?

options.label: thunder is shy
options.why: Thunder has no feelings. Light is just faster than sound.

options.label: our ears are slow
options.why: Our ears work fine. Sound just moves slower than light.

rounds.explain: Light travels much faster than sound, so the flash reaches us first.
rounds.hint: Think about which is faster, light or sound.
